question: Which of the following groups of organisms help in keeping the environment clean?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bacteria and Fungi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bacteria and fungi play a crucial role in decomposition**, breaking down organic matter into simpler substances, recycling nutrients back into the ecosystem.
 
• These microorganisms help in **waste degradation**, cleaning up dead plants, animals, and other organic waste present in the environment.
 
• Fungi, especially saprophytic fungi, decompose cellulose and lignin from plant matter, ensuring the breakdown of tougher organic compounds.
 
• Bacteria assist in the **bioremediation of pollutants**, including oil spills, heavy metals, and toxic chemicals, thereby improving environmental health.
 
• Both bacteria and fungi are essential in maintaining the ecological balance by **converting waste into usable resources** such as compost and humus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Decomposition:**

 
 
• Decomposition is the process by which organic substances are broken down into simpler organic or inorganic matter.
 
• It is primarily carried out by microorganisms such as bacteria and fungi.
 
• This process is essential for nutrient cycling in ecosystems.
 
 
 
• **Bioremediation:**
 
 
• Bioremediation is the use of microorganisms to degrade environmental contaminants.
 
• Bacteria and fungi are key agents in cleaning up pollutants like oil spills and heavy metals.
 
• This method is eco-friendly and cost-effective for restoring polluted environments.
 
 
 
• **Role of Fungi:**
 
 
• Fungi are saprophytic organisms, meaning they feed on dead and decaying matter.
 
• They break down complex organic compounds such as cellulose and lignin.
 
• Fungi also form symbiotic relationships, such as mycorrhizae, aiding in plant nutrient absorption.
 
 
 
• **Role of Bacteria:**
 
 
• Bacteria are involved in nitrogen fixation, converting atmospheric nitrogen into forms usable by plants.
 
• They assist in composting by breaking down organic waste into nutrient-rich soil additives.
 
• Some bacteria, like Pseudomonas, are effective in cleaning oil spills and other toxic pollutants.
